title: Incremental promotion API: transaction-safe model promotions with deterministic exposure controls
creator: Priya Patel
description: Problem: teams need a deterministic, transaction-safe way to promote model versions incrementally across user cohorts (canary, A/B, shadow) while preserving idempotency and enforceable permissions. Current SDK helpers are ad-hoc and surface race conditions when concurrent promotions occur. Goal: design and ship an API + client helper patterns that let callers create a promotion transaction, attach deterministic exposure controls (hashing keys + holdback percentage), support shadow mirroring, and provide automatic rollback triggers backed by telemetry. The API must be permission-gated, support idempotency tokens for safe retries, and return clear reconciliation outcomes for orchestrators.
acceptance_criteria: Client helper library (JS + Go) supports: beginPromotion(), previewExposure(seed,user_id), commitPromotion(id, idempotency_key), abortPromotion(id)
Deterministic exposure: callers can specify exposure_key (e.g., user_id) and holdback_percentage (0-100) and preview API returns consistent bucket assignment
Idempotency behavior: POST to commit with same idempotency token is safe and returns same terminal state
Permission model: rollout.write required to begin/commit; rollout.approve required for promotions >10% or cross-region rollouts
Automatic rollback: configurable triggers (error-rate delta, latency p95, quality-regression) can be attached to a promotion and will transition to ABORT when breached
Telemetry hooks: promotion-level metrics (exposure_count, errors_by_model, latency_p95_by_variant) emitted to console and available via query API
E2E test coverage for concurrency edge cases and rollback path
implementation_notes: Design promotion as a two-phase transaction: CREATE (staging) -> PREVIEW -> COMMIT/ABORT
Store deterministic bucketing config: hashing algorithm (xxhash64), salt (seed), and exposure_key path
Idempotency: require client-supplied idempotency_token for commit/abort; server stores terminal decision keyed by token+promotion_id
Conflict resolution: if two commits arrive concurrently, the first token wins; subsequent commits with different tokens return 409 with current terminal state and suggestion to reconcile
Shadowing: support mirror=true flag that routes a copy of requests to candidate without affecting exposure counts
Permissions: new scopes rollout.create, rollout.commit, rollout.approve; wire into RBAC checks in control plane
Schema: promotion object includes id, model_versions, exposure_config (key, percentage, seed), telemetry_triggers, created_by, state, created_at, updated_at
api_examples:
GET /v1/promotions/prom_abc123/preview?user_id=U-549  --> {"assignment": "candidate", "bucket_hash": 0.0412, "exposed": false}
(consistent across calls for same user_id + seed)
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (API design + security): define wire contracts and RBAC scopes; review with security and infra
Phase 2 (server impl): implement two-phase promotion state machine and deterministic bucketing in control plane
Phase 3 (SDK): ship JS + Go helpers with preview and idempotency helpers
Phase 4 (observability): hook promotion-level metrics into console and add runbook for rollback
Phase 5 (beta): opt-in beta with 3 pilot customers and internal end-users
Phase 6 (GA): enable self-serve in console and document audit trails
telemetry_requirements: Emit promotion.* metrics: promotion.created, promotion.committed, promotion.aborted
Sampling: full sampling for first 5k exposures, then 1% thereafter unless debug mode
Audit logs: record actor, idempotency_token, and API caller IP on state transitions
qa_checks: Concurrent commit/abort fuzz tests (confirm first-wins semantics)
Deterministic bucketing regression tests with different seeds and keys
Permission matrix tests for rollout.create / rollout.commit / rollout.approve
End-to-end mirror tests that validate mirrored requests do not change production counters
Rollback trigger simulation that causes telemetry breach and verifies automatic abort executes
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: incorrect bucketing causing biased exposure -> Mitigation: deterministic hashing library + cross-language test vectors
Risk: idempotency collisions leading to surprising results -> Mitigation: require cryptographically-strong idempotency_token and surface clear 409 responses
Risk: permission escalation for high-percentage promotions -> Mitigation: require rollout.approve for >10% or multi-region promotions
Risk: telemetry lag preventing timely rollback -> Mitigation: allow a hybrid mode that uses local-inference health signals for fast failover
